The economic replication bundle in the preceding v0.6.0 release supplies de-identified transformed inputs, fitted models and six exact-output reproduction cases for the native policy-fee task. abstract: Wind-power events connect atmospheric variability to operational decisions, but their useful information depends on measurement and representation. We introduce a protocol-aware framework linking structural survival, independent physical tracking and forecast-to-cost validation across eight archives, 340 turbines and seventeen detector configurations. Ordered trajectories preserve transferable structure among matched, encodable events, while polarity protection restores a distinction erased by angular encoding. Reconstructing independently measured wind trajectories reveals where temporal information matters most. For power-defined compound events, scale-restored trajectories reduce reconstruction error by 11.7% and 24.5% against strong scalar controls at two light detection and ranging (LiDAR) instruments, with positive paired seven-day confidence intervals. Internal-geometry error falls by 9.6–26.9% across both instruments and a French WindCube population. Separately, historical shape and issued weather inputs support an 18.2% reduction in simulated four-hour accuracy charges relative to persistence under a documented Jiangsu rule. These findings establish event complexity and decision objectives as guides to representation design, connecting transferable structure to physical interpretation and economic evaluation.
highlights: Protocol-aware measurement links event structure, physical tracking and cost.
Ordered trajectories reduce compound wind-process errors by 11.7% and 24.5%.
Internal wind-geometry errors fall by 9.6–26.9% across three references.
Polarity protection isolates a recoverable ambiguity in angular encoding.
A shape-and-weather forecast pipeline cuts rule-based four-hour charges by 18.2%.
